request.user:
Subject: Physics
Question type: single-correct (exactly one option is right)

A resistance of 40 ohm and an inductance are connected in series in a 50 cycles/second ac circuit. The impedance of this combination is very nearly
(A) 30 ohm
(B) 40 ohm
(C) 50 ohm
(D) 60 ohm

result.value: Z ≈ 50 Ω (only if L = 95.5 mH, as in the standard version of this problem)
result.working: Z = √(R² + X_L²), where X_L = 2πfL. The value of L is not given, so Z cannot be found from the stated data. All we can say is Z > 40 Ω, which rules out (A) and (B). In the standard version of this problem, L = 95.5 mH. Then X_L = 2π(50)(0.0955) ≈ 30 Ω. Z = √(40² + 30²) = 50 Ω, which is option (C).
result.note: The question does not give the inductance value, and it is needed to compute X_L and Z. The answer C assumes the standard textbook value L = 95.5 mH. Without L, either (C) or (D) could be correct.
